clue.text: Rattling good advice to secure a catch

definitions.text: Rattling good advice to secure a catch

parts.words: Rattling good advice to secure a catch
parts.note: split the answer into three words and it is the tip a fisherman would give for landing fish; the whole is a clicking percussion instrument, hence 'Rattling'

explanation.surface: A tip for an angler hoping to land a fish, described as excellent advice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rattling good' reads as old slang for 'very good', but 'Rattling' points to the clicking hand-held instrument, while the rest reads as the phrase cast a net.
explanation.definitionFit: The instrument is a pair of clicking wooden shells, so it makes a rattling noise, and casting a net is how you secure a catch.

clue.text: Hue from St. Peter's over the Eternal City?

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece written over another comes before it

parts.note: St Peter's is a church, abbreviated CH
Rome is traditionally called the Eternal City

explanation.surface: A colour seen from St Peter's Basilica looking out across Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: Chrome yellow and chrome green are pigments, so the word names a colour or shade.

clue.text: Reaper appearing out of sorts to the French

parts.note: feeling out of sorts means feeling unwell or ill
le is French for 'the'

explanation.surface: Someone harvesting looks unwell next to the French.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved hand blade for cutting corn is a reaping tool, so it can be called a reaper.

clue.text: Screen artists given a right start

indicators.note: the A and R are placed at the beginning, before the artists

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, so artists are RAS

explanation.surface: Painters are handed a correct beginning for their screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given a right start' means A and R go in front of RAS.
explanation.definitionFit: An arras is a tapestry wall hanging, which can serve as a curtain or screen, as in Hamlet.

clue.text: Jewel of small type

definitions.meaning: printers once named type sizes, and this one was about six and a half points

explanation.definitionFit: The green gemstone is a jewel, and old printing gave the same name to a small size of type between nonpareil and minion.

clue.text: Darling of the hit parade?

parts.note: split into POP and PET it reads as a favourite of the pop charts; as one word it is a term of endearment

explanation.surface: A singer who is a favourite of the music charts.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'hit parade' is the pop chart, so a darling of it is a pop pet.
explanation.definitionFit: A dear little person is called a little darling, an affectionate word for a child.

clue.text: Sort of respect afforded Bacon, I see

indicators.note: to sort letters is to arrange them, so the words that follow are rearranged

explanation.surface: Sir Francis Bacon is shown a particular kind of deference, I notice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of' rearranges BACON, I and SEE; 'afforded' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A bow or curtsey is a gesture of deference, a show of respect.

clue.text: Settle in writing for later payment

definitions.text: Settle in writing for later payment

parts.words: Settle in writing for later payment
parts.note: to settle a bill by writing a cheque dated in the future, so it cannot be cashed until later

explanation.definitionFit: Putting a future date on a cheque means it is settled in writing but paid only later.

clue.text: Scientific practice that puts a burden on part of the economy

parts.note: to tax someone is to put a burden on them

indicators.note: only a portion of the word economy is used, its last three letters

explanation.surface: A scientific method that loads costs onto a sector of the economy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part of' takes OMY from the end of 'economy'.
explanation.definitionFit: The classification of living things into ranked groups is a scientific discipline.

clue.text: Being a judge is also instrumental

definitions.meaning: in England a part-time judge in the Crown Court has this title
a wooden flute played by schoolchildren is a musical instrument

explanation.definitionFit: A part-time English criminal judge holds this title, and the end-blown flute is a musical instrument.

clue.text: Former kingdom wherein different sexes get the point

parts.note: W, west, is a point of the compass

indicators.note: different signals the letters of sexes are made into something else

explanation.surface: An old realm where men and women each get the point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' turns SEXES into ESSEX, after the compass point W.
explanation.definitionFit: This Anglo-Saxon realm in south-west England was one of the old kingdoms before England united.

clue.text: Looks up and down

indicators.note: a down entry that reads the same upwards as downwards, letter for letter

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A glance up and down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up and down' says the four letters read the same either way along a down light.
explanation.definitionFit: To look at something is to observe it with the eyes.

clue.text: Refreshment taken after some agitation

parts.note: a drink made by vigorously whisking dairy with flavouring, so it is drunk after being agitated

explanation.definitionFit: The frothy dairy drink is a refreshment that is literally shaken before serving.

clue.text: One could be carried if chairmen upheld it

definitions.text: One could be carried if chairmen upheld it

parts.words: One could be carried if chairmen upheld it
parts.note: chairmen here are the bearers of a covered chair carried on poles, who hold it up and carry a passenger

explanation.definitionFit: The covered chair on poles was borne by two porters known as chairmen, carrying its passenger.

clue.text: Chopin's second and last love, by George!

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An exclamation about Chopin's final romance.
explanation.walkthrough: The French novelist George Sand was Chopin's last lover; 'by George!' is both an exclamation and the pen name.
explanation.definitionFit: The writer Aurore Dupin used the pen name George and was the composer's final partner.

clue.text: Like the story about an old English act, maybe

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the letters following are rearranged

explanation.surface: Like a tale concerning a piece of old English legislation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges AN, OLD, E and ACT; 'maybe' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A short tale of an incident is a personal account, so something based on such tales is like the story.

clue.text: Can and must find somewhere private

indicators.note: the letters of the two words must be worked over to find something new

explanation.surface: You can and must locate a private place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'find' asks for a new word from CAN and MUST.
explanation.definitionFit: An inner sanctuary is a private retreat where one is not disturbed.

clue.text: He may judge one stupid to spray roses

parts.note: a stupid person is an ass

indicators.note: a spray of flowers is loose and scattered, so the word roses is rearranged

explanation.surface: A judge, possibly a fool, hoses down some roses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spray' makes ESSOR from ROSES, after ASS.
explanation.definitionFit: An evaluator who gives a judgement on value or quality, as at an exam or a flower show.

clue.text: Large number having fun with a net, possibly

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, a large number
ragging is boisterous fun or teasing, as in a student rag

explanation.surface: Lots of people enjoying themselves with a net.
explanation.walkthrough: Ragging is British for horseplay, as in a student rag week.
explanation.definitionFit: Hauling a net along the bottom of a river or pond is trawling, one way of searching.

clue.text: Sorry about the bridge-builder's spelling

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so sorry is wrapped around the other piece

parts.note: CE stands for civil engineer, who builds bridges

explanation.surface: An apology concerning an engineer's spelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spelling' means casting spells, not writing words.
explanation.definitionFit: Casting spells is witchcraft or magic.

clue.text: Still one myth not proven

parts.note: still means yet, as in 'not yet'
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Still, one legend remains unproven.
explanation.definitionFit: The abominable snowman of the Himalaya is a creature of legend whose existence is unproven.

clue.text: Arrangement of late carrying weight in China

indicators.note: an arrangement puts letters in a new order, so late is rearranged

explanation.surface: Something placed recently, carrying weight in China.
explanation.definitionFit: A Chinese unit of weight, also used of silver as money.

clue.text: What may be seen on the line between Norfolk and Lincs.

definitions.text: What may be seen on the line
definitions.meaning: washing hung on a clothes line
the bay on England's east coast between the counties of Norfolk and Lincolnshire

explanation.definitionFit: Laundry pegged out on a clothes line, and the shallow North Sea inlet between Norfolk and Lincolnshire, two English counties.

clue.text: Misconception causing anger on the motorway

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece on top of another comes before it

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's first motorway, written MI
rage is fury or anger

explanation.surface: A false belief causing road rage on the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the London-to-Leeds motorway; its 1 is read as I.
explanation.definitionFit: An optical illusion in hot air makes one think water is there, a false impression.

clue.text: Suffering sappers encountered in small ways

indicators.note: the sappers are placed inside the other letters

parts.note: STS is short for streets, ways
the Royal Engineers, RE, are known as sappers

explanation.surface: Soldiers encountered hardship in small ways.
explanation.walkthrough: Sappers are the Royal Engineers, RE, set within STS and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Strain or pressure causing distress or hardship.

clue.text: Snicked to the boundary

definitions.meaning: in cricket, nicked off the bat's side
bordered, with a fringe at the edge

explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a ball snicked off the side of the bat has been nicked, and a garment bordered is given a trim.

clue.text: Having taken the blame at first she'll treat you

parts.note: taken as written
to take the rap is to take the blame
first is 1ST, written IST

explanation.surface: Having accepted responsibility at first, she will look after you.
explanation.walkthrough: 1ST is the shortened 'first', its 1 read as I.
explanation.definitionFit: A counsellor or practitioner treats patients for illness or problems.

clue.text: Wide-awake as the elusive ratel

indicators.note: elusive implies the word ratel slips into a new form

explanation.surface: Watchful as the honey badger that escapes capture.
explanation.walkthrough: A ratel is the honey badger.
explanation.definitionFit: Watchful and attentive means fully awake.

clue.text: A hero cult notion so confined

indicators.note: the word so holds the other piece within it

parts.note: taken as written
a hint is a slight notion or suggestion

explanation.surface: A belief in heroes is presented as a confined idea.
explanation.definitionFit: Japan's native religion venerates ancestors and kami, including deified heroes.

clue.text: Brave description of an old enemy

definitions.text: Brave description of an old enemy

parts.words: Brave description of an old enemy
parts.note: a brave is a Native American warrior; this is the term such a warrior was said to use for a white settler

explanation.definitionFit: In Westerns, Native Americans called white settlers by this term for their light skin.

clue.text: Talk about wind!

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a gale is a strong wind

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a lot of hot air.
explanation.definitionFit: To entertain someone with lengthy anecdotes is to talk at them amusingly.

clue.text: Indications of a closed shop

parts.note: not the trade-union sense, but the panels pulled down over a shop window when it closes

explanation.definitionFit: Panels drawn over windows show a shop is closed for the day.
